transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-28 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Mills (Redwood AE), Priya Narang (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Alex Romero (CTO, Neptune), Samira Lee (ML Engineer), Marcus Grant (Infra), Tina Park (SRE)

Summary: quick run through of the regression symptoms, then deep dive into runtime traces and a proposed bisect/test harness for quant-induced accuracy drops.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Jordan from Redwood, gonna hand over to Priya and we'll dig into the quant findings.
[00:12] Alex: yeah hi, thanks. We saw a noticeable drop on about 8% of our evaluation set after switching to the int8 gpt-q path, plus the cold starts spiked on the first 10 requests.
[00:23] Priya: ok, clear. Priya here, I'm the SE on this, we'll go through both the accuracy and the runtime stuff. Couple clarifying q's first — are you running the on-prem package behind your V-P-C with the Redwood private agent or is this the Dedicated route?
[00:40] Samira: we're on our on-prem kubernetes cluster, vpc peering to the control plane. Using local GPUs with the Redwood private runtime.
[00:47] Priya: got it. that helps. Marcus, are you applying any custom kernel or patched CUDA on your fleet?
[00:52] Marcus: nothing custom, stock drivers from our vendor, but we do have NCCL tuned and a small patch for pcie error handling.
[00:58] Luis: quick note — sometimes PCIe or driver diffs cause subtle timing differences that can make kv cache populate slightly differently, worth noting.

[01:10] Jordan: ok let's walk through the symptoms. Samira shared a deck and a short log — jordan/link: tinyurl.com/np-quant-deck (note: link posted in chat). The two main issues: 1) accuracy regressions after int8/gptq quantize on 8% prompts; 2) cold-start latency for first 8 tokens is 2.5x higher than baseline.

[01:35] Samira: yeah the accuracy ones are weird — in some cases completions are hallucinating payment amounts, sometimes truncation at the end. It's not consistent with sequence length, seems prompt-dependent.

[01:48] Priya: ok can you give an example of a failing prompt?
[01:51] Samira: sure I'll share, here's a short list — we have 50 failing prompts in the shared bucket. Some of them only fail if kv cache wasn't warmed by a prior context — suggests a kv coherence issue.

[02:10] Priya: interesting, so you might be hitting a KV staleness or a sticky-kv warmup pathway. A couple of notes from the runtime side: when we do INT8 or AWQ conversions sometimes the attention kernel ordering and fused ops differ which changes the timing of KV writes into the cache — on small batches that can lead to the first few tokens missing cached prefixes, producing a different internal state.

[02:40] Alex: hmm ok. Is that a known pathology with the g-p-t q path?
[02:43] Priya: there are known micro-diffs yes — g-p-t-q converters (GPTQ) and AWQ have different rounding/quantization strategies per-layer, and for some models that interacts poorly with our KV cache warmup heuristics. It's not the majority but it shows up on edge prompts.

[03:00] Marcus: also we saw cold-start throughput drop when container is busy and we have a high tail in scheduling, sometimes the first request waits for a warmup compile. Are you pre-compiling kernels in your on-prem runtime?

[03:14] Luis: we do JIT-like kernel selection; the first sequence length can trigger a different kernel. We have a kernel cache but on clean nodes there's a compile/warm path. That explains latency spikes.

[03:30] Priya: right, so two orthogonal problems: (A) runtime cold-start/compilation and kernel selection causing latency, (B) quantization-induced semantic drift via layerwise rounding and kv warmup ordering. We'll tackle both.

[03:50] Jordan: let's go into the data. Priya, can you share the profile?

[03:54] Priya: sharing screen — ok here's the timeline: first 8 tokens show high time in attention kernel selection and cache fill. After ~12 tokens things stabilize. The logs also show some mismatched sequence hash for certain prefixes, which is suspicious — that could be caused by an off-by-one in the attention fusion after quantization.

[04:20] Samira: do you think it's an actual algorithmic change (e.g. different softmax behavior) or just numeric noise?

[04:26] Priya: likely a mix. GPTQ tends to preserve model behavior but rounding can change logits by small deltas; for prompts near decision boundaries that can flip generation paths. AWQ has different scale tables and sometimes introduces bias if we don't calibrate using representative activations.

[04:45] Alex: we tried per-layer fallback to fp16 on layers 0..2 and didn't fully remove the regression — it reduced, but some prompts still fail.

[04:55] Priya: that's expected. Some failures originate in middle layers where KV state is written; fallback of early layers helps but you may need selective fallback (e.g., layers 6,9). We have tooling to recommend layer subsets via sensitivity scanning.

[05:12] Luis: we should run a layer-sensitivity sweep; it graphs delta-accuracy vs cost for each layer when forced to FP16. It's part of Redwood Optimize recommendations.

[05:25] Jordan: Samira we can run that for you and produce a heatmap. Action item: Priya will prepare the sensitivity sweep harness.

[05:34] Samira: great. On the cold start side — we saw a handful of instances where the first request triggered a kernel fallback to a slow path — sometimes due to missing MKL/cuBLAS libs on our nodes. Could missing vendor libs cause different kernels to be chosen?

[05:48] Priya: yes vendor libs and driver versions matter. Also our runtime will choose different fused kernels if it detects FP8 vs INT8 paths. On first invocation the kernel selection code probes and may compile a fallback kernel. If your nodes are slightly resource constrained that can delay the first token.

[06:10] Marcus: note we do boot some containers with limited gpushares early in the morning for batch jobs; maybe the first real request sees contention. We can isolate by reserving one GPU for inference.

[06:22] Alex: from a product perspective our SLO is p95 < 200ms for interactive flows and the cold-starts are blowing that on the first interaction.

[06:31] Jordan: ok, practical mitigations: 1) pre-warm instances with a lightweight warmup script that calls a low-cost prompt to populate kv and trigger kernel cache; 2) enable sticky hot containers (reserve a pool) for high-traffic endpoints; 3) apply targeted per-layer fallback based on sensitivity sweep.

[06:52] Priya: adding to that — we also recommend KV sticky prefetching: when a session starts, fetch common prefixes across likely intents to prepopulate KV. It's a tradeoff vs memory but helps cold-start.

[07:05] Samira: how invasive is the prefetch hooking? Will we need code changes?

[07:09] Priya: minimal — it's a config + small middleware call we can provide. We'll share the snippet.

[07:16] Luis: another nuance — batching size and batch alignment affects KV coherence. If you're sending variable-length single-request batches the runtime may reorder micro-batches for throughput, which can expose kv race conditions with certain quant kernels.

[07:33] Marcus: we saw reordering on peak, yeah. Our queue tries to fill to max batch but the latency SLO forces a smaller batch.

[07:42] Priya: you can configure batching thresholds and per-endpoint latency budgets; also sticky-kv affinity helps so related requests hit the same worker and sequentially populate cache.

[07:55] Alex: ok enough theory — what's the reproducible bisect plan?

[07:58] Priya: plan: we run the same seed set with three quant paths: GPTQ, AWQ, and int8 native. For each path we run: (a) cold-clean node test (no kernel cache), (b) warm node test, (c) sticky-kv prefetch, and (d) per-layer fallback toggles. We'll collect token-level logits, hashes, and final outputs. Then run a diff and cluster failing prompts.

[08:22] Samira: good — can you add a run where we force kernel selection to the same path (disable JIT) so we can separate compile variance from numeric variance?

[08:29] Priya: yes we can add a deterministic kernel mode in the harness. That will isolate compile/JIT effects.

[08:35] Jordan: Priya, timeline?

[08:37] Priya: I'll have the harness and instructions by 2027-01-04. We'll include a small public repo and a docker image to run locally.

[08:45] Samira: I'll ingest the harness and run on our staging k8s cluster next week. Marcus will coordinate node reservations.

[08:51] Marcus: yep I can reserve a nodepool with identical driver versions.

[08:56] Alex: we also need compliance and security docs before we flip the Dedicated pilot — can you attach SOC2/ISO docs?

[09:02] Jordan: yes we'll send the compliance pack and the Private deployment checklist.

[09:07] Luis: small technical detail — when logging kv writes we sometimes scrub small float differences out. For bisect we should capture raw fp16/INT8 scaling factors as stored, not just final logits.

[09:19] Priya: agreed. we'll add raw scaling factors and per-layer quant tables to the artifact uploads.

[09:25] Samira: question on AWQ — is AWQ deterministic? We saw slightly different outputs between runs even on warm nodes.

[09:31] Priya: AWQ is deterministic given same RNG seed and kernel path, but if kernel selection or threading differs across runs you can get divergence. We'll force single-threaded attention for a run to confirm.

[09:43] Alex: any known model-specific gotchas? We're using a custom finetuned Llama-3 derivative.

[09:49] Priya: finetuned heads and adapted embeddings sometimes amplify quant errors if the finetune used small learning rates; those layers can be more sensitive. We should check layerwise activation ranges.

[09:59] Samira: ok we'll dump activation histograms for a few batches.

[10:03] Priya: excellent. Next, I want to call out the KV cache staleness hypothesis: when a prefixed context is truncated early the kv pointers might not align across mixed-precision paths — that can flip attention maps. We'll instrument sequence hashes at the write/read points to confirm.

[10:20] Marcus: can you script the instrumentation? We can run on our staging nodes to collect the traces.

[10:24] Priya: yes, in the harness we'll add a kv-trace mode that logs per-layer kv write indices and the computed seq hash.

[10:33] Jordan: perfect. Any objections to us starting with AWQ path then GPTQ, or should we prioritize int8?

[10:40] Samira: we prefer starting with GPTQ since that's what our pipeline switched to originally, then test AWQ and native int8 for comparison.

[10:46] Priya: fine. We'll prioritize GPTQ.

[10:49] Luis: also recommend running a short FP8 baseline if you can — some models perform better with limited FP8 mixed precision than INT8 due to dynamic range.

[10:58] Alex: we don't currently have FP8 toolchain in our infra, is that heavy lift?

[11:03] Priya: it's a moderate lift — drivers and certain kernels need FP8 support. Redwood can supply a container with FP8 libs if you want to try in staging.

[11:10] Samira: yes please provide that container.

[11:13] Jordan: noted — supply FP8 container.

[11:18] Priya: ok wrapping towards runbook — deliverables from Redwood: (1) bisect harness repo + docker image, (2) sensitivity sweep script and recommended layer fallback heatmap, (3) FP8 test container, (4) compliance pack and Dedicated pilot pricing. From Neptune: (a) failing prompts, (b) run results from staging + kernel logs, (c) confirm nodepool and reservation window.

[11:40] Samira: timeline — we can run initial staging tests 2027-01-06 to 2027-01-08, then reconvene for a 2-hour triage on 2027-01-10.

[11:50] Jordan: ok I'll block 2 hours on Jan 10 — Priya and Luis will be on the call.

[11:55] Alex: thanks everyone. Quick operational question: any impact on cost if we fallback many layers to fp16?

[12:02] Priya: yes there is unit cost impact — more FP16 increases memory and latency and may reduce throughput. Our sensitivity heatmap will show tradeoffs; often 2-4 layer fallbacks restore accuracy with small perf penalty.

[12:15] Marcus: ok we'll be conservative.

[12:18] Jordan: final recap: Priya prepare harness by Jan 4, Samira upload 50 failing prompts by Dec 31, Jordan send pricing and compliance by Dec 30, schedule Jan 10 triage. Any other items?

[12:31] Tina: please include runbook for hot-container warmup script.

[12:36] Priya: will do.

[12:39] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links.

[12:43] Alex: thanks team.

[12:45] End of meeting.

Notes on transcript quality: speaker labels sometimes approximate; some product names were auto-transcribed (gptq -> g p t q, kv -> k-v, etc). Artifacts shared in chat: tinyurl.com/np-quant-deck, s3://neptune-quant/failing-prompts-2026-12-27.zip, drive.redwood/quant-harness.
